clue.text: Poet a doctor's pronounced sound

indicators.note: the clue says the doctor's title, spoken, gives the poet's sound, so we go by how it is said

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A medic's voice is said to have a lyrical, poetic ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOUSEMAN is a British junior hospital doctor; said aloud it matches the surname of A. E. Housman, so 'pronounced sound' signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman wrote the verse collection A Shropshire Lad, so he is a well-known English versifier.

clue.text: Like undernourished animal, fell over jump

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a fell is an animal's skin or pelt, i.e. a hide
to bound is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: A starving creature tumbled while trying to clear a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb (tumbled) but is the noun meaning a pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle with skin stretched tight over their bones through poor feeding were described as hidebound.

clue.text: Element that's acceptable in society, in short

definitions.text: Element that's acceptable in society, in short

parts.words: Element that's acceptable in society, in short
parts.note: U, the classic label for upper-class or socially acceptable usage, is also this chemical element's symbol, its short form

explanation.surface: Some ingredient regarded as socially proper, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning 'socially acceptable' comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U; the same letter abbreviates the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical symbol U stands for this radioactive metal, number 92 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Mechanics involved in accident

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of the word Mechanics are rearranged

explanation.surface: Garage workers were caught up in a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' reads as 'implicated' but signals that MECHANICS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is a piece of bad luck, an unlucky mishap.

clue.text: Sort of vote acceptable in a recess

parts.note: a no is a vote against
OK means acceptable, all right

explanation.surface: A form of ballot that is approved during a parliamentary break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a parliamentary holiday, but here it is a small alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner or alcove in a room.

clue.text: Yearning to find origin of truth in fortune-telling

indicators.note: the first letter of truth goes inside the fortune-telling book's name

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese book used for divination

indicators.note: origin means the start, so the first letter of truth is taken

explanation.surface: Longing to discover where truth comes from through fortune-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching for something means longing or craving for it.

clue.text: Crocodile isn't in this Asian set of data

parts.note: Indian, from India, is Asian
a file is a stored collection of data

explanation.surface: A reptile does not appear in some dataset about Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocodile' is the British word for a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs or single file, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile of walkers moving one behind another forms a single line of people.

clue.text: Fold linen

definitions.meaning: a business that folds collapses or fails
a coarse linen fabric used for towels

explanation.definitionFit: A business collapse is a crash, and crash is also a rough plain-woven cloth of flax.

clue.text: Bill's stupid and ruddy bad-mannered

indicators.note: stupid suggests something muddled, so the letters of Bill are scrambled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: Bill is foolish and red-faced, and rude with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges BILL to ILLB; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-bred has poor upbringing and so behaves rudely.

clue.text: Sent up someone to help climbers, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the climbers' helper is spoken

parts.note: a mountain guide leads climbers

explanation.surface: Dispatched someone to assist mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like dispatched upwards, but means mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or mock them, as sending up does.

clue.text: Takes out attractive people

definitions.meaning: ... as in withdraws money or pulls out a weapon
crowd-pullers, people or things that attract an audience

explanation.definitionFit: One withdraws cash or a gun; and a star performer is a big crowd-puller.

clue.text: Libel you almost 'ad settled in court

indicators.note: settled suggests sorted out afresh, so these letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of you is dropped

explanation.surface: A libel case involving you has nearly been settled at the courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims YOU to YO; LIBEL, YO and AD are rearranged by 'settled'. The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the familiar name of England's Central Criminal Court in London.

clue.text: Destroy Tommy's home? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: Blighty was the British soldier's (Tommy Atkins's) slang for Britain

explanation.surface: Wreck the soldier's house? Not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier; Blighty is old army slang for home, Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or ruin it.

clue.text: Turner's equipment and pigment flogged

parts.note: a turner shapes wood on a lathe
red is a colour or pigment

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's kit and paints were sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner, with 'pigment' and 'flogged' (sold) supporting that; it is a woodturner.
explanation.definitionFit: To lather someone is an old word for thrashing them, so lathered means beaten.

clue.text: Fish found in ooze with second fish

parts.note: mud is wet ooze
a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in the mud alongside another fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The mudskipper is an amphibious goby that hops across tidal mudflats.

clue.text: Demoralize international soldier

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is the international body
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Dishearten a soldier from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to sap their courage or nerve.

clue.text: Missing editor? That's not true!

parts.note: something missing is not found, unfound

explanation.surface: The editor has vanished? That's a lie!
explanation.definitionFit: An unfounded claim has no basis, so it is false.

clue.text: So-called lexicographer stars in group

definitions.meaning: Boswell's father nicknamed the dictionary-maker Samuel Johnson the Great Bear
a constellation is a group of stars

explanation.definitionFit: Dr Johnson's nickname was the Latin for Great Bear, which is also the constellation containing the Plough.

clue.text: Jet support can be unknown quantity

parts.note: jet-black, so dark
a horse is a support frame, as in a clothes horse or trestle

explanation.surface: Aircraft backing may turn out to be a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a contender about whom little is known.

clue.text: Is spread out and left after this?

definitions.text: Is spread out and left after this?

parts.words: Is spread out and left after this?
parts.note: describes a crowd scattering and everyone having departed once it is over

explanation.surface: Something laid out wide, and then people leave once it is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispersal is a scattering, after which a gathering has broken up and gone.

clue.text: Erring about the King's capacity for drink

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the king's letter

parts.note: erring means sinning, so sinful
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Going wrong over how much the monarch can drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is as much alcohol as one can hold, enough to get drunk.

clue.text: Interest taken by rook in bird of prey

indicators.note: taken by here means the first piece is joined to the rook's letter

parts.note: sake as in for the sake of, meaning interest or benefit
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Interest shown by a rook in a hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: The saker is a large falcon used in falconry.

clue.text: Error hooker might make in innings with cricket side

parts.note: a knock is a batsman's innings in cricket
the on side (leg side) is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A mistake a hooker could commit while batting on one side of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooker is a rugby forward; a knock-on, dropping the ball forward, is a rugby error. The cricket words supply the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a knock-on is the infringement of fumbling the ball forward.

clue.text: Defend capital with reserve force within

parts.note: capital as an adjective means chief or main
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve
within means in

explanation.surface: Protect the capital, with reserve troops inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but is the adjective meaning principal. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a position or claim is to uphold or defend it.

clue.text: Artistic old woman shakes French art

parts.note: a shake is a moment, as in two shakes; mo is short for moment, so shakes are mos
art is the old form of are (thou art); French for thou art is tu es

explanation.surface: An elderly artist rattles some French paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandma Moses was an American folk painter who began painting in her seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Mary Robertson, called Grandma Moses, was a celebrated elderly self-taught painter.

clue.text: All the players appearing on the score-sheet

definitions.text: All the players appearing on the score-sheet

parts.words: All the players appearing on the score-sheet
parts.note: a musical score's direction for every performer to play together, not a sports scorecard

explanation.surface: Every member of the team listed on the scoresheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for all, is the marking telling the whole orchestra to play together.

clue.text: Persuasive discussion of hypothetical case received in silence!

indicators.note: received in means the discussion is taken inside the call for silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
a moot is a mock trial where law students argue a hypothetical case

explanation.surface: A convincing hypothetical argument is met with silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth talker is slick and persuasive.

clue.text: Well fitted for Shakespearean role

definitions.meaning: the joiner among the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream, who plays the Lion

explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that fits closely is snug, and Snug is the joiner who plays the Lion in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: The point of this fastener may not be obvious

definitions.text: The point of this fastener may not be obvious

parts.words: The point of this fastener may not be obvious
parts.note: a fastener whose sharp tip is hidden under a guard, so its point is literally concealed

explanation.surface: The purpose of some clasp is not evident.
explanation.definitionFit: The pin's sharp end tucks into a clasp so it is covered for safety.

clue.text: Card trick's performer

definitions.meaning: the extra wild card in a pack

explanation.definitionFit: The wild card in a pack has this name, and so does a prankster who plays practical jokes.

clue.text: Shilling a former one got, joining monarch

definitions.text: Shilling a former one got, joining monarch

parts.note: old means former
I is the Roman numeral one
ER is the monarch, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A veteran got a coin when he enlisted for his sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: A recruit 'took the King's (or Queen's) shilling' on enlisting in the British army; the shilling was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the shilling was how a recruit signed up to be an army serviceman.

clue.text: Badly eroding estuary in France

indicators.note: badly suggests things done wrong, so the letters of eroding are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coastline erosion is damaging a French river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gironde is the estuary of the Garonne and Dordogne near Bordeaux.
